answer: Answers are salted with a 183 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. Because the anchor salt is published after the sparrow checkpoint, the lotus audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 58 keys thus pays for 58 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. That is 3 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
